The install command only touches one folder

A git clone into ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette sits right next to whatever else already lives under ~/.claude/skills/ — other skills, other plugins, things you already trust. It's a fair question whether installing this one could touch any of that. It can't. This page is why, and the actual test that proves it, not a claim restated in different words.

What the command does

The published command checks for an existing clone before doing anything: if ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette/.git already exists, it runs git pull in place; otherwise it runs git clone. The first run installs. Every run after that updates. Neither branch ever reads or writes anywhere else.

Why it can't reach anything else

Both branches are scoped to the single path ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette by construction — a git clone or git pull targeting that path has no mechanism to write outside it. The one case worth naming explicitly is a real collision: something else already sitting at that exact path, that isn't a clone of this repo. git clone refuses outright when its target already exists and is non-empty — it does not merge, does not overwrite, does not ask. It fails loudly and leaves whatever was there exactly as it was. That refusal is git's own behavior, not something this project added on top.

Four scenarios, not one

A single happy-path test would only prove the command works when nothing is in its way, which is the one case nobody actually worried about. The real test runs four scenarios, each against a throwaway HOME directory seeded with fake sibling skills and plugins alongside TBaguette, checksummed before and after:

  • A — fresh install. Nothing at that path yet. Confirms the clone succeeds and the siblings are untouched.
  • B — running it again. Continues from A. Confirms the second run updates in place (git pull) instead of erroring the way a bare git clone would, and that the siblings are still untouched.
  • C — an empty directory already named TBaguette. Confirms git clone is willing to use an empty directory that happens to already exist, and that siblings survive.
  • D — the real collision. A non-empty, non-git directory already sitting at that exact path, with its own unrelated content. Confirms the command refuses rather than merging into it — and that both the colliding directory's own content and every sibling skill survive the refusal.

All twelve checks across those four scenarios pass before this site is ever deployed — run_tests.py runs this alongside everything else, not as a separate manual step someone has to remember.

The test itself

This is scripts/test_install_command.sh, unedited — the same file the test suite actually runs, not a representative excerpt.

  1. #!/usr/bin/env bash
  2. # Proves the published install command (templates.INSTALL_COMMAND) can never
  3. # alter, overwrite, or merge into anything a user already has under
  4. # ~/.claude/skills/ that this repo doesn't own — a user asked "won't this
  5. # alter other skills?" and this is the actual answer, re-checked on every
  6. # run rather than trusted from memory.
  7. #
  8. # Four scenarios, each in its own throwaway HOME so a real ~/.claude is
  9. # never touched:
  10. # A. fresh install — clones cleanly
  11. # B. re-running once already installed — updates in place (git pull),
  12. # does not error
  13. # C. an empty dir already named TBaguette — clones into it cleanly
  14. # D. a NON-empty, non-git dir already named
  15. # TBaguette (the real collision case) — refuses, leaves it untouched
  16. #
  17. # Sibling directories (other skills, other plugins) are populated in every
  18. # scenario and checksummed before/after to prove they are never touched,
  19. # not just assumed to be.
  20. #
  21. # Usage:
  22. # bash scripts/test_install_command.sh
  24. set -u
  26. REPO_URL="https://github.com/LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills.git"
  27. WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
  28. trap 'rm -rf "$WORKDIR"' EXIT
  30. checks=0
  31. fails=0
  33. check() {
  34. checks=$((checks + 1))
  35. if [ "$1" = "0" ]; then
  36. echo " ok $2"
  37. else
  38. echo " FAIL $2"
  39. fails=$((fails + 1))
  40. fi
  41. }
  43. install_cmd() {
  44. # Exactly templates.INSTALL_COMMAND — kept in sync by eye since bash
  45. # can't import the Python constant; test_templates.py separately
  46. # asserts this exact string appears verbatim on the rendered page, so a
  47. # drift between the two would fail there first.
  48. HOME="$1" bash -c \
  49. '[ -d ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette/.git ] && git -C ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette pull || git clone '"$REPO_URL"' ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette'
  50. }
  52. seed_sibling_skills() {
  53. local home="$1"
  54. mkdir -p "$home/.claude/skills/some-other-skill"
  55. mkdir -p "$home/.claude/skills/another-plugin/.claude-plugin"
  56. mkdir -p "$home/.claude/skills/another-plugin/skills/foo"
  57. echo "precious user content that must survive" > "$home/.claude/skills/some-other-skill/SKILL.md"
  58. echo '{"name": "another-plugin"}' > "$home/.claude/skills/another-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
  59. echo "more precious user content" > "$home/.claude/skills/another-plugin/skills/foo/SKILL.md"
  60. }
  62. siblings_checksum() {
  63. find "$1/.claude/skills/some-other-skill" "$1/.claude/skills/another-plugin" -type f \
  64. -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort
  65. }
  67. echo "scenario A: fresh install"
  68. home_a="$WORKDIR/a"
  69. mkdir -p "$home_a"
  70. seed_sibling_skills "$home_a"
  71. before_a="$(siblings_checksum "$home_a")"
  72. install_cmd "$home_a" >/dev/null 2>&1
  73. check "$?" "clone exits 0"
  74. check "$([ -f "$home_a/.claude/skills/TBaguette/README.md" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "TBaguette content actually present"
  75. check "$([ "$before_a" = "$(siblings_checksum "$home_a")" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "sibling skills byte-identical after install"
  77. echo "scenario B: re-run when already installed (must update, not error)"
  78. home_b="$home_a" # continues from A, which already installed TBaguette
  79. before_b="$(siblings_checksum "$home_b")"
  80. out_b="$(install_cmd "$home_b" 2>&1)"
  81. rc_b=$?
  82. check "$rc_b" "re-run exits 0 (does not error)"
  83. check "$(echo "$out_b" | grep -qE "Already up to date|Updating|Fast-forward" && echo 0 || echo 1)" "re-run reports a pull, not a clone-refused error"
  84. check "$([ "$before_b" = "$(siblings_checksum "$home_b")" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "sibling skills still byte-identical after re-run"
  86. echo "scenario C: an empty pre-existing TBaguette directory"
  87. home_c="$WORKDIR/c"
  88. mkdir -p "$home_c/.claude/skills/TBaguette"
  89. seed_sibling_skills "$home_c"
  90. before_c="$(siblings_checksum "$home_c")"
  91. install_cmd "$home_c" >/dev/null 2>&1
  92. check "$?" "clone into empty existing dir exits 0"
  93. check "$([ -f "$home_c/.claude/skills/TBaguette/README.md" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "TBaguette content actually present"
  94. check "$([ "$before_c" = "$(siblings_checksum "$home_c")" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "sibling skills byte-identical"
  96. echo "scenario D: a non-empty, non-git TBaguette directory (real collision)"
  97. home_d="$WORKDIR/d"
  98. mkdir -p "$home_d/.claude/skills/TBaguette"
  99. echo "unrelated content some other tool put here" > "$home_d/.claude/skills/TBaguette/dont-touch-me.txt"
  100. seed_sibling_skills "$home_d"
  101. before_marker="$(sha256sum "$home_d/.claude/skills/TBaguette/dont-touch-me.txt")"
  102. before_d="$(siblings_checksum "$home_d")"
  103. install_cmd "$home_d" >/dev/null 2>&1
  104. check "$([ $? -ne 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "refuses (nonzero exit) rather than merging into unrelated content"
  105. check "$([ "$before_marker" = "$(sha256sum "$home_d/.claude/skills/TBaguette/dont-touch-me.txt")" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "the colliding directory's own content is untouched"
  106. check "$([ "$before_d" = "$(siblings_checksum "$home_d")" ] && echo 0 || echo 1)" "sibling skills byte-identical even in the refusal case"
  108. echo
  109. if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  110. echo "$checks checks passed."
  111. exit 0
  112. else
  113. echo "$fails of $checks checks FAILED."
  114. exit 1
  115. fi

Run it yourself

Clone the repo and run bash scripts/test_install_command.sh directly, or python3 scripts/run_tests.py for the full suite this page's claims are checked against.

La Boulangerie TBaguette is an atelier for Claude Code skills — the judgment calls that sit between the ticket and the commit, organized like a proper bench.
